As per the office report, notice has been issued to respondent no. 2, which is reported to be served on him but none has appeared on behalf of respondent no. 2 nor any counter affidavit is filed.

The present petition has been filed by the petitioner against the summoning order dated 14.11.2017 passed by learned Judicial Magistrate-I, Hapur in Complaint Case no. 500 of 2017 (Ajab Singh vs.
Manoj Kumar and others) under Section 420 IPC, P.S. Dhaulana, District Hapur whereby petitioner and co-accused Ajab Singh (respondent no. 2) are summoned to face trial for charge under Section 420 IPC; the petitioner has preferred criminal revision against the summoning order, which was also dismissed by the impugned order dated 25.7.2022 passed by learned Sessions Judge, Hapur in Criminal Revision no. 42 of 2022; both orders of the courts below are challenged in the present petition.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned AGA for the State.

The brief facts of the present case is that an FIR was lodged at the instance of informant Ajab Singh on 1.7.2011, which was registered as Crime no. 165 of 2011, under Sections 420, 406 IPC, P.S.

1 Dhaulana, District Ghaziabad against petitioner and two others with allegation that place of in-laws of Manoj was lying in village of informant; at the instance of Manoj Kumar, accused Raj Kumar and his father Kheta met the informant and offered a job for his son if the informant manages Rs. 03 lakhs for that; informant also informed some of his relatives, who are in need of job; the informant got Rs. 4,29,000/- deposited ICICI Bank account of Raj Kumar lying in Ghaziabad.

entities.text: Kheta Ram Saini @ Kheta vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However,
accused persons got untraceable for three months after receiving the said amount; police investigated the case and filed first final report in the matter in favour of the named accused persons, to which, protest petition was filed by the informant wherein learned Magistrate directed for further investigation under Section 173(8) Cr.P.C.; police again filed final report after further investigation and and a protest petition was again filed by the informant wherein learned Magistrate fixed the case for recording statement of witnesses under section 200/202 Cr.P.C. and learned court issued process u/s 82 Cr.P.C. against accused Manoj Kumar, Raj Kumar and Kheta to face trial under Section 420 IPC.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that even if the FIR version and statement of the witnesses recorded u/s 200/202 Cr.P.C. is taken on its value, there is no averment that the said amount was paid to the petitioner; in FIR and in statement of witnesses this fact is emerged that amount of Rs. 4,29,000/- was credited in the account of accused Raj Kumar, who is son of the petitioner; petitioner has nothing to do with the matter; police investigated the matter twice and found the FIR version to be non reliable and submitted final report in favour of accused persons.

However, trial court has summoned the accused persons including the petitioner on the basis of statements of the complainant and witnesses without considering the fact that no independent witness has been produced in support of the FIR version and alleged witnesses are father and sons in relation; no offence is made out against the present petitioner on the basis of materials on record.

Per contra, learned AGA submitted that first final report is of 14.7.2012; it is stated that investigation is concluded with finding that dispute between parties is found to be of borrowing of money and in absence of evidence, investigation is closed.

He further submits that summoning order was challenged by one of the accused Kheta only and no revision is filed by accused Manoj Kumar and Raj Kumar; the accused Raj Kumar is son of the petitioner, who is shown as beneficiary of the alleged transaction.

In the FIR version as well as in the statement of witnesses, this fact has emerged that amount of Rs. 4,29,000/-, which belongs to the informant and his acquaintances, was credited to account of Raj Kumar, who is son of the petitioner and this fact is also emerged in the FIR as well as statement of witnesses that present petitioner was hand in glove with said Raj Kumar and he also visited the informant alongwith Raj Kumar where negotiation regarding payment of money and assurance of job for son of informant and other was given by them.

It is disputed question of facts, which cannot be gone into while deciding present petition filed under Article 227 of the Constitution of India; on perusal of materials available on record, I do not find it to be a fit case for exercising jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution of India.
Petition lacks merits and is liable to be dismissed.
The writ petition is dismissed, accordingly.
